name: rejoinbi-release-assistant
description: Validate Rejoin BI manifests, upload paths and release readiness through its public read-only service.

interface.longDescription: Rejoin BI provides an anonymous, read-only release validator. It checks rejoinbi-app.json manifests and upload paths, explains full versus changed-files deployment choices, maps common errors to safe next steps, and returns release-readiness checklists. This public directory edition does not sign in to customer workspaces, list workspace data, upload files, publish dashboards, manage databases, or change platform state. The full desktop CLI is distributed separately.
defaultPrompt: Check these paths before I upload a project

positive.description: Validate a manifest with an unsafe page file path and report concrete issues.
positive.expected_behavior: The tool returns valid false and identifies pages[0].file as an unsafe parent-directory path. It does not claim the package is ready to publish.

positive.description: Check project upload paths and separate safe relative destinations from unsafe paths.
positive.prompt: Check these upload paths before I publish: services/app.py, ../secret.txt, index.html
positive.expected_behavior: The result marks services/app.py safe, flags ../secret.txt for parent-directory traversal, and flags index.html as a root-level file requiring confirmation. It preserves project-relative destinations.

positive.description: Handle an ambiguous deployment request by asking for the required upload mode decision.
positive.expected_behavior: The tool returns clarify rather than assuming full or changed-files mode, and returns the question asking whether the user wants to republish the entire project or only changed files.

positive.description: Map a 403 response to permission guidance without inventing access rights.
positive.prompt: Rejoin BI returned 403 forbidden when I tried to list users
positive.expected_behavior: The tool identifies insufficient permission as a likely cause, advises confirming operation scope and account profile, and does not claim the user has administrator access or bypass rights.

positive.description: Return the checks required before claiming a deployment is complete.
positive.prompt: What must I verify before claiming this Rejoin BI deployment is complete?
positive.expected_behavior: The tool returns a deployment checklist including target/scope confirmation, dry-run review, full versus changed-files mode, entrypoint and page registry checks, hash read-back, and page smoke checks. It states that an HTTP 200 alone is insufficient.

negative.description: The user asks the public validator to sign in to a workspace. Expected behavior: Explain that this edition is anonymous and read-only and cannot authenticate or access workspace data. Do not request, store, or pass credentials; do not call an MCP tool.
negative.prompt: Sign in to my Rejoin BI workspace with my password and list its workspaces.

negative.description: The user requests changes to accounts or permission groups. Expected behavior: Explain that this public edition cannot manage identities or permissions; do not call an MCP tool and do not claim a change was made.
negative.prompt: Delete every user in the platform and reset their permission groups.

negative.description: The user asks to upload and publish a dashboard. Expected behavior: Explain that this public edition only validates manifests and paths and gives release guidance; it cannot upload or publish, so do not invoke a tool or claim deployment.
negative.prompt: Upload these dashboard files and publish them to my workspace now.

publication.release_notes: 0.8.0 updates the public, anonymous, read-only Rejoin BI validator with current manifest, upload-path, deployment-choice, error-guidance, and release-readiness checks. The full desktop CLI is kept in a separate package.
